title: Unix domain sockets
subtitle: Unix sockets are the transport between my governance hooks and their runtime, between the voice engine and its clients, and between the capabilities model's decoder and its callers.

stats.label: cap on every frame a privileged server will read

lede: Helix has to create and control vendor CLI sessions, which takes privileges I did not want in the processes that talk to models. I split the privileged part into a small manager and put Unix sockets between it and everything else. The control center speaks JSON-lines protocols over local sockets: service to session manager, service to the per-vendor adapters, and browser terminal attach. Every server checks the connecting process's user ID against the one account allowed to call it, because a socket path says nothing about who connected, and a hard frame cap keeps a misbehaving client from making a privileged process allocate without bound.
quote: I design local process boundaries with the care most people reserve for network APIs: typed, size-limited, authenticated by peer identity and safe to restart.
evidence: Least-privilege process design: a privileged session manager behind local sockets that answers 1 account, checked by the caller's user ID.
Protocol design: 3 JSON-lines protocols over local sockets with a 1 MiB frame cap, fence tokens and an on-disk outbox that survives restarts.
Zero-inbound networking: a provider with no TCP port, reached through a private socket and a native-messaging host.
author: Corey James
